# Voting maps {#sec-voting}

Happy post-election day.  

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Today we'll make some voting maps to visualize election results a few different ways.
:::

## Install and load libraries

```{r}
#| label: install cartogram
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

install.packages('cartogram')
install.packages('ggthemes')

```


```{r}
#| label: load libraries
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(cartogram)
library(tigris)
library(ggthemes)

```

## Maps from R-Graph-Gallery

We will make 4 types of election maps.

We'll use the ideas from [r-graph-gallery](https://r-graph-gallery.com/map.html)

- regular ggplot map  
- cartogram    
- bubble  

### Data 

County-level 2024 election results for the US are [here](https://github.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24/blob/master/2024_US_County_Level_Presidential_Results.csv).  

```{r}
#| label: read_data
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

pres2024 <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24/refs/heads/master/2024_US_County_Level_Presidential_Results.csv')

head(pres2024)

```

Load county geospatial data from tigris.

```{r}
#| label: read_counties
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

US_counties <- counties(cb = TRUE, year = 2024, progress_bar = FALSE) 

head(US_counties)
```

### Tidy and Join data for maps

Let's try a left join of the geospatial data using the `county_fips` and `GEOID` columns. We could also try by county name, but that is less good due to duplicates of names.  

```{r}
#| label: join_county
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

countyVotes <- inner_join(US_counties, pres2024, by = c('GEOID' = 'county_fips')) |> 
  select(GEOID, NAME, votes_gop, votes_dem, total_votes, diff, per_point_diff, geometry, STUSPS) |> 
  mutate(percent_diff = 100*per_point_diff)

head(countyVotes)
```

### Basic map

```{r}
#| label: basic US county map
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

ggplot(data = countyVotes) +
  geom_sf() +
 # scale_fill_gradient2(low = 'blue', mid = 'white', high = 'red', midpoint = 0) + ##Manual gradient for fill to make a traditional map
  theme_map() + #from ggthemes
  coord_sf(xlim =c(-124, -65),
           ylim = c(25, 50)) 
```

### Chloropleth map - binned

```{r}
#| label: basic chloropleth map
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

countyVotes |> 
  mutate(color = ifelse(diff>0, 'red', 
                       ifelse(diff < 0, 'blue', 'white'))) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = color)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('blue', 'red'), ) +
  theme_map() + #from ggthemes
  coord_sf(xlim =c(-124, -65),
           ylim = c(25, 50))+
  theme(legend.position = 'none')

```

## Gradient chloropleth map

```{r}
#| label: Gradient map
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

ggplot(data = countyVotes, aes(fill = percent_diff)) +
  geom_sf() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = 'blue', mid = 'white', high = 'red', midpoint = 0) + ##Manual gradient for fill to make a traditional map
  theme_map() + #from ggthemes
  coord_sf(xlim =c(-124, -65),
           ylim = c(25, 50)) +
  labs(fill = '% vote difference')
```

### Bubble map

First, we need to make lat and lng columns for the county to center the bubbles on.

```{r}
#| label: Coordinates
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

tempTbl <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(countyVotes)) ## create an arry of centroid coordinates  
countyVotes$lng <- tempTbl[,1] ## assign longitude coordinate
countyVotes$lat <- tempTbl[,2] ## assign latitude coordinate
```


```{r}
#| label: Bubble map
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

ggplot(data = countyVotes) +
  geom_point(aes(x = lng, y = lat, size = total_votes, color = percent_diff)) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = 'blue', mid = 'grey90', high = 'red', midpoint = 0) + ##Manual gradient for fill to make a traditional map
  theme_map() + #from ggthemes
  coord_sf(xlim =c(-124, -65),
           ylim = c(25, 50)) +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')

```

### Cartogram

Land doesn't vote - people do.  Let's squeeze the map to show people. Unfortunately, it is slow, so we'll just do it for California. 

First we need to do some cartographic transformations.

```{r}
#| label: Cartogram crs transform
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

# need first to "change" the projection to Mercator (AKA Google Maps): EPSG: 3857
ca_merc <- countyVotes |> 
  filter(STUSPS == 'CA') |> 
  st_transform(3857)

ca_cartogram <- cartogram_cont(ca_merc, "total_votes", itermax = 15)

# And back to the previous projection
ca_cartogram <- st_transform(ca_cartogram, st_crs(countyVotes)) #or use 4269 for crs


```

```{r}
#| label: Cartogram US vote map
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

ggplot(data = ca_cartogram, aes(fill = percent_diff)) +
  geom_sf() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = 'blue', mid = 'white', high = 'red', midpoint = 0) + ##Manual gradient for fill to make a traditional map
  theme_map() + #from ggthemes
  labs(fill = '% difference')

```
